answer: Given data: \\ Resistance per coil, $R = 8\text{ }\Omega$ \\ Reactance per coil, $X_L = 6\text{ }\Omega$ \\ Line voltage, $V_L = 440\text{ V}$ \\ Connection: Star \\ \\ **1. Phase Impedance ($Z_{ph}$):** \\ $$Z_{ph} = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ }\Omega$$ \\ \\ **(i) Phase Current ($I_{ph}$):** \\ Phase voltage $V_{ph} = \frac{V_L}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{440}{\sqrt{3}} = 254.03\text{ V}$ \\ $$I_{ph} = \frac{V_{ph}}{Z_{ph}} = \frac{254.03}{10} = 25.4\text{ A}$$ \\ \\ **(iii) Line Current ($I_L$):** \\ For a star connection, $I_L = I_{ph} = 25.4\text{ A}$. \\ \\ **(iv) Power Factor ($\cos\phi$):** \\ $$\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z_{ph}} = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8\text{ (lagging)}$$ \\ \\ **(ii) Total Active Power ($P$):** \\ $$P = \sqrt{3} V_L I_L \cos\phi = \sqrt{3} \times 440 \times 25.4 \times 0.8 = 15461.3\text{ W} = 15.46\text{ kW}$$
proTip: Always compute the phase impedance and power factor first in AC circuit problems to simplify subsequent current and power calculations.
